section_summary: The section closes an alphabetical index of Japanese manufacturers, then contains a July 1945 Foreign Economic Administration study of Japan’s merchant shipping, including statistical tables and methodological appendices. Later correspondence concerns translations of Japanese plastics reports and motor scooter production; a January 1948 telegram reports bicycle chain export orders, capacity, specifications, and price.

subfiles.title: Alphabetical index of Japanese manufacturers, H–Y
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese manufacturing firms with reference numbers.
subfiles.summary: The closing pages of an alphabetical manufacturer index list firms from Hitachi through Yoshita with numerical references.

subfiles.title: The Volume and Character of Japan’s Merchant Shipping
subfiles.doc_type: classified research report with tables and appendices
subfiles.from: Foreign Economic Administration, Enemy Branch, Japanese Special Services Staff
subfiles.about: Assesses prewar and wartime Japanese merchant shipping and estimates potential postwar coastal carrying capacity.
subfiles.summary: The report compares Japan’s 1931–40 merchant fleet, prewar vessel employment and cargo movements with wartime losses and changes in ship size, speed, and routes. It estimates remaining carrying capacity on representative coastal runs and identifies policy questions for postwar shipping controls. Tables document vessels, tonnage, cargo, and capacity; appendices define navigation areas and explain statistical methods. Page 598 is a repeated or supplementary cover preceding the methodological appendices.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese plastics report translators
subfiles.from: W. T. Crase, Society of the Plastics Industry
subfiles.about: Requests names of commercial Japanese translators in Washington for War Department plastics reports.
subfiles.summary: The society seeks translators for Japanese-language reports on Japan’s plastics industry.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Japanese plastics translations
subfiles.from: Mia L. Martin, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Responds to the request for translators and mentions an apparently English-language report.
subfiles.summary: The department cannot provide translator names and points to a report believed to be in English.

subfiles.title: Cushman inquiry about Japanese motor scooters
subfiles.from: D. B. Sayre, Cushman Motor Scooter Sales Co.
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Raises concern that Japanese motor scooter engine production might support aircraft engine manufacture.
subfiles.summary: Sayre forwards an attachment and asks the department to investigate Japanese scooter production and engine sources.

subfiles.title: Reply to Cushman concerning Japanese motor scooters
subfiles.from: Charles L. Hodge, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds that permitted Japanese industrial activity is under Allied consideration.
subfiles.summary: Hodge acknowledges Cushman’s concern and says Allied planning will address prevention of Japanese rearmament.

subfiles.title: Bicycle chain production and export commitments
subfiles.about: Reports committed Japanese bicycle chain exports, expected production, specifications, and dollar price.
subfiles.summary: Export production through November is committed to orders for India, Singapore, and the United States; output depends on coal and materials.
